knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Aeration on a drought-stressed lawn can slow recovery and cause damage. The correct response defers the service, records the reason and agrees a reassessment date.
Services and heads must be marked and the depth tested before deeper settings are used, to avoid damaging sprinkler heads and buried services.
These services involve skill, equipment, waste and aftercare. They are priced for those components and quoted separately from routine mowing.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock lawn with a drought-stress card, the learner recommends deferral or proceeding with a stated reason, within the assessor's set time.
The learner marks at least two mock sprinkler heads on a supplied mock lawn and sets the aerator depth on a test strip before the assessor allows full use.
The learner completes a quote sheet for a supplied mock aeration scope that separates labour, equipment, waste and aftercare.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Signed diagnosis and deferral record for the mock lawn.
Assessor observation record of the marking and depth test.
Quote sheet for the mock scope, reviewed by the assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Use of the aerator on a mock lawn in drought stress during the assessment.
Use of deep tines near a marked mock sprinkler head.
Leaving simulated plugs or thatch on the mock lawn at the end of the task.
